bugs.name: New tag dialog is titled Edit Tag
bugs.summary: The create-tag dialog uses the Edit Tag heading even when launched from Add New Tag with an empty Name field.
bugs.expected: The dialog for creating a tag should be titled Add New Tag or Create Tag.
bugs.actual: Settings > Tags > Add New Tag opens a blank-name dialog headed Edit Tag.
reproSteps: Sign in and open Settings > Tags.
Click Add New Tag.
Observe that the blank-name dialog is headed Edit Tag.

bugs.name: API Keys Learn More link opens wiki Home instead of API Keys documentation
bugs.summary: The API Keys section’s Learn More link opens the Uptime Kuma wiki Home page instead of API Keys guidance.
bugs.expected: The Learn More link in the API Keys settings section should open documentation about API Keys.
bugs.actual: Clicking Learn More opened a new tab at https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/wiki/ showing the Home page, not API Keys documentation.
reproSteps: Open Settings > API Keys as the fixture admin.
Click Learn More.
Observe that the linked API-Keys wiki URL redirects to the wiki Home page.

bugs.name: Disabled proxy reopens with Enabled turned on
bugs.summary: A proxy saved with Enabled off reopens in edit mode with Enabled on. Reconfirmed by closing and reopening the same fixture; its host and port matched and the switch remained on.
bugs.expected: After saving a proxy with Enabled off, editing that proxy should show Enabled off, consistent with the setting and its help text describing activation status.
bugs.actual: Saved the fresh proxy mo-proxy-20260414-84729.invalid:3128 with Enabled off. On two openings of that same proxy's edit dialog, Enabled was checked on; Set As Default and Apply on all existing monitors remained off.
reproSteps: Open Settings > Proxies and create a disposable HTTP proxy with a unique hostname and port.
Turn Enabled off and save.
Edit the saved proxy; Enabled is checked again.

bugs.name: Uncolored tags are unreadable in the Tags list
bugs.summary: A tag saved without a selected color has no readable name in the Tags list; the same row remains nameless after canceling deletion.
bugs.expected: A successfully saved tag's name remains visibly readable in its Tags list row even when no color is selected, including after canceling deletion.
bugs.actual: The uncolored tag row showed its 0 Monitors count and delete control, but no readable name with the pointer away from the row. After choosing No in the delete confirmation and waiting six seconds, the name was still not visible. The accessibility snapshot retained the tag name; hovering the row only made faint white text appear against the highlight.
reproSteps: Open Settings > Tags and create a disposable tag without selecting a color.
Observe that its Tags list row shows 0 Monitors and a delete control but the tag name is invisible.

bugs.name: The proxy activation helper text contains an incorrect word and ungrammatical instructions.
bugs.summary: The proxy activation helper text contains an incorrect word and ungrammatical instructions.
bugs.expected: Helper text should use correct wording to clearly explain when the proxy affects monitor requests and how to disable it.
bugs.actual: The dialog says, “This proxy will not effect on monitor requests until it is activated. You can control temporarily disable the proxy from all monitors by activation status.”
reproSteps: Open Settings > Proxies > Set Up Proxy.
Read the Enabled helper text, which says not effect on monitor requests and control temporarily disable.

bugs.name: Contradictory Monitor History retention guidance for 0 days
bugs.summary: Entering 0 makes the Monitor History explanation simultaneously state that data is kept for 0 days and that 0 means infinite retention; the contradictory text persists after blur. Restored the original 180 value without saving.
bugs.expected: When the retention value is 0, the explanation identifies this as infinite retention without also claiming monitor history is kept for 0 days.
bugs.actual: At value 0, the visible explanation reads: “Keep monitor history data for 0 days. Set to 0 for infinite retention.” It remained unchanged after the field was blurred and after waiting; the initial explanation at 180 read “Keep monitor history data for 180 days. Set to 0 for infinite retention.”
reproSteps: Open /settings while signed in as the authorized admin account using the provided saved-auth session; no authentication details were changed.
Open the Monitor History settings section and note that the retention field is 180 and the explanation says history is kept for 180 days, with 0 for infinite retention.
Replace the retention value with 0 without pressing Save; observe the explanation say history is kept for 0 days and that 0 means infinite retention.
Blur the field and wait; verify the same contradictory explanation remains visible.
Restore the field to 180 without pressing Save.

bugs.name: Stacked error notifications cover confirmation buttons and intercept clicks
bugs.summary: Error toasts remain above confirmation dialogs. With several persistent monitor failures, stacked notifications cover Yes and prevent clicking monitor deletion confirmations until the notifications are dismissed.
bugs.expected: Confirmation dialogs and their action buttons remain above background notifications and can be clicked.
bugs.actual: Yes cannot be clicked because a Vue-Toastification error toast intercepts the pointer at its center. The button was at x734.6,y165 with size67.8×38, and hit testing returned the error toast. Closing the toasts makes Yes clickable and deletion succeeds.
reproSteps: Sign in at a 1280×900 viewport with the default persistent error-notification timeout.
Create several test monitors targeting closed localhost ports so their error notifications stack at the right side of the page.
Without reloading or dismissing the notifications, open a monitor and click Delete.
Try to click Yes in the confirmation dialog.
Dismiss the overlapping error notifications using their close buttons and try Yes again.

reviewedVariants.name: Monitor-error toasts obscure the Don't expire checkbox in the API Key dialog
reviewedVariants.summary: Red monitor-error toast notifications stack over the open API Key dialog and obscure the “Don't expire” checkbox; a tap while it is covered does not select it.
reviewedVariants.expected: The Add API Key dialog should leave its expiry controls usable so the administrator can select “Don't expire” before generating a key.
reviewedVariants.actual: At 390×844, red monitor-error toasts stacked over the dialog, including the checkbox area. A tap while obscured left the checkbox unchecked; when unobstructed in an earlier attempt, one tap toggled it. No key was generated.
reproSteps: Open /settings/api-keys at a 390×844 viewport, authenticated as an administrator using the provided session.
Click Add API Key and enter the fresh name exp-apikey-toast-overlay-20260615-a61p. Do not click Generate.

When red monitor-error toasts stack over the dialog, tap the “Don't expire” checkbox once. It remains unchecked while covered; the toasts visibly obscure the control. Leave the dialog unsaved and do not generate a key.

matchingGuidance.acceptanceScope: Accepted as a valid reference by user instruction; source prerequisites and remaining evidence gaps are retained below.
prerequisites: Multiple error toasts overlap an open modal at the reported viewport.
